Agamemnon (Ancient) was a king of Mycenae who commanded the Achaeans during the Trojan War.

This early-20th-century Indian rebel leader took up ascetic renunciation at 18 and added a name in memory of a lost love, before leading a famous jungle uprising against British colonizers — who is he?
Alluri Sitarama Raju (4 July 1897 or 1898 - 7 May 1924) was an Indian revolutionary who waged an armed rebellion against the British colonial rule in India.
Before serving as a government minister overseeing sport and broadcasting, this four-time member of India's parliament led the country's cricket governing body from 2015 to 2017 — who is he?
Anurag Thakur (born 24 October 1974) is an Indian politician from the Bharatiya Janata Party and a Member of Parliament in the Lok Sabha from Hamirpur, Himachal Pradesh.

Fought over two days in June 1314 between Robert the Bruce and England's Edward II, this decisive Scottish clash during the siege of a royal castle became a turning point in the fight for independence — which clash?

Battle of Bannockburn (Scottish) was fought on 23-24 June 1314, between the army of Robert the Bruce, King of Scots, and the army of King Edward II of England, during the First War of Scottish Independence.

Traditionally credited to an 8th-century BCE prophet but believed by modern scholars to blend the work of at least three authors across centuries, which text opens the major prophets of the Christian Old Testament?
Book of Isaiah is the first of the Latter Prophets in the Hebrew Bible and the first of the major prophets in the Christian Old Testament.
Flying the Spirit of St. Louis alone for over 33 hours to win the $25,000 Orteig Prize, this aviator completed the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in May 1927 — who is he?
Charles Lindbergh (February 4, 1902 - August 26, 1974) was an American aviator, military officer, and author.

This Anatolian mother goddess, with a possible forerunner in Neolithic Çatalhöyük, had her Phrygian cult adopted by Greek colonists and spread across the Greek world by the sixth century BC — who is she?
Cybele is an Anatolian mother goddess; she may have a possible forerunner in the earliest Neolithic at atalhyk.
Nicknamed after a Renaissance artist, this Ukrainian soldier became the youngest battalion commander in his country's military history while leading a right-wing volunteer movement — who was he?
Dmytro Kotsiubailo (1 November 1995 - 7 March 2023) was a Ukrainian volunteer, soldier, lieutenant, a commander of the 1st Mechanized Battalion of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
Convicted of war crimes at Nuremberg, this German grand admiral commanded the Kriegsmarine until 1943, when Karl Dönitz took over — who is he?
Erich Raeder (24 April 1876 - 6 November 1960) was a German admiral who played a major role in the naval history of World War II and was convicted of war crimes after the war.
The only Central African president born in modern-day Gabon, this former army chief led the country from 2003 to 2013 — who is he?
François Bozizé (born 14 October 1946) is a Central African politician who was President of the Central African Republic from 2003 to 2013.

Gloria Macapagal Arroyo (born April 5, 1947), often referred to as PGMA or GMA, is a Filipino academic and politician who served as the 14th president of the Philippines from 2001 to 2010.

Commissioned into a light horse unit his own father raised, he became the first Australian to reach lieutenant general and led the Desert Mounted Corps to one of military history's fastest pursuits. Who was this WWI commander?

Harry Chauvel (16 April 1865 - 4 March 1945) was a senior officer of the Australian Imperial Force who fought at Gallipoli and during the Sinai and Palestine Campaign in the Middle Eastern theatre of the First World War.

Founded in 2021 by former presidential candidate Muharrem İnce after splitting from the country's main opposition, this movement echoed the spirit of Atatürk in its slogan and dissolved itself in 2025 — what was it called?

This Spanish politician has served as president of the Community of Madrid since 2019, and also leads the regional branch of Spain's People's Party — who is she?
Isabel Díaz Ayuso (born 17 October 1978) is a Spanish politician who has served as the president of the Community of Madrid since 2019.

A Democratic attorney and Army National Guard officer who served in Kandahar Province, this North Carolina official became the state's 52nd attorney general in 2025 after previously representing its 14th congressional district — who is he?
Jeff Jackson (politician) (born September 12, 1982) is an American politician, attorney, and Army National Guard officer who has served as the 52nd attorney general of North Carolina since 2025.
When he finally stepped down in 2017, he was Africa's second-longest-serving president — the man who led Angola and its ruling MPLA for nearly four decades. Who is it?
José Eduardo dos Santos (Portuguese; 28 August 1942 - 8 July 2022) was an Angolan politician and military officer who served as the second president of Angola from 1979 to 2017.

Generally credited with commissioning the Great Pyramid of Giza, this Fourth Dynasty pharaoh who succeeded his father Sneferu survives in only one complete portrait — a tiny ivory figurine. Who is he?
Khufu was the second pharaoh of the Fourth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning during the 26th century BC in the early Old Kingdom period.
The first president of Ukraine, he led the country to independence from the Soviet Union and oversaw the handover of its nuclear arsenal before an economic crisis cost him re-election — who was he?
Leonid Kravchuk (10 January 1934 - 10 May 2022) was a Ukrainian politician who served as the first president of Ukraine from 5 December 1991 to 19 July 1994.
This economist-turned-politician became Moldova's first female president in 2020, after previously serving as prime minister for a few months in 2019 — who is she?
Maia Sandu (born 24 May 1972) is a Moldovan politician and economist who, since 2020, has served as the sixth president of Moldova.
This Royal Navy navigator led the first inshore circumnavigation of mainland Australia and championed the very name "Australia" as "more agreeable to the ear." Who was he?

Matthew Flinders (16 March 1774 - 19 July 1814) was an English Royal Navy officer, navigator and cartographer who led the first inshore circumnavigation of mainland Australia, then called New Holland.
Spending most of his career in Kuwait's security and intelligence services and once the world's oldest crown prince, this royal became Emir of Kuwait at age 83 in 2023 — who is he?
Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah (born 27 September 1940) is Emir of Kuwait, reigning since 2023.
This ongoing rural conflict between India's government and communist guerrilla factions traces back to a 1967 village uprising that fractured the Communist Party of India — what is it known as?
Naxalite–Maoist insurgency is an ongoing conflict between the Government of India and left-wing extremist groups.

Flourishing in what is now Veracruz and Tabasco from roughly 1200 to 400 BC, this early Mesoamerican civilization relocated its center from San Lorenzo to La Venta after the former's decline — who were they?

A Rhodes Scholar and Harvard graduate who once worked at McKinsey, this politician served as mayor of South Bend, Indiana, before becoming the 19th U.S. secretary of transportation — who is he?
Pete Buttigieg (born January 19, 1982) is an American politician and former naval officer who served as the 19th United States secretary of transportation from 2021 to 2025.
On this recurring April Fools' social experiment, registered users could color a single pixel on a shared online canvas, then had to wait minutes before placing another — what's the Reddit project?
R/place was a recurring collaborative project and social experiment hosted on the content aggregator site Reddit.
This explorer became the first person in history to walk to both the North and South Poles, and later founded an organization dedicated to preserving Antarctica — who is he?
Robert Swan (born 28 July 1956) is the first person to walk to both poles.

This Spanish politician has led the far-right party Vox since founding it in 2014, and now also presides over the pan-European Patriots.eu alliance, having earlier served in the Basque Parliament as a centre-right legislator. Who is he?
Santiago Abascal (born 14 April 1976) is a Spanish politician who has been the president of Vox, a far-right political party, since 2014.
Varieties of this political philosophy differ by how much they rely on markets versus planning, but all favor social ownership of production over private — which ideology is it?
Socialism is an economic and political philosophy encompassing diverse economic and social systems characterised by social ownership of the means of production, as opposed to private ownership.
Representing Massachusetts in the U.S. Senate from 1962 until his death in 2009, this Democratic lawmaker was the younger brother of a president and a U.S. attorney general — who was he?
Ted Kennedy (February 22, 1932 - August 25, 2009) was an American lawyer and politician who represented Massachusetts in the United States Senate from 1962 until his death in 2009.

Akhmad Kadyrov: Chechen militant and revolutionary (1951–2004)

French Fourth Republic: Government of France from 1946 to 1958. It also saw the beginning of the rapprochement with France's longtime enemy Germany, which led to Franco-German co-operation and eventually to the European Union.

George W. Bush: President of the United States from 2001 to 2009.

India–Pakistan war of 1965: Armed conflict. Much of the war was fought by the countries' land forces in Kashmir and along the border between India and Pakistan.

Jacob Rothschild, 4th Baron Rothschild: English peer, investment banker and philanthropist (1936–2024)

A former police officer who rose to deputy commissioner, this politician was the sole candidate approved by Beijing in the 2022 election that made him Hong Kong's chief executive — who is he?
John Lee Ka-chiu: Chief Executive of Hong Kong since 2022. After Carrie Lam became chief executive in 2017, Lee was promoted to secretary for security.
This Roman military commander proclaimed himself dictator for life in 44 BC before being dramatically removed from power—by his own senators. Who was he?
Julius Caesar: Roman general and dictator (100–44 BC)

Krupp family: German dynasty from Essen. The Krupp family is a prominent 400-year-old German dynasty from Essen, noted for its production of steel, artillery, ammunition and other armaments.

Merlin: Legendary Welsh wizard. Geoffrey's account presented Merlin as a prophet and royal advisor to Arthur's father, Uther Pendragon.
This ancient Levantine kingdom along the Dead Sea's eastern shore is known from the Mesha Stele, which records its victory over a son of Israel's King Omri — what was it?
Moab: Ancient kingdom East of the Dead Sea. Moab was an ancient Levantine kingdom whose territory is today located in southern Jordan.

Active from 1929 to 1941, this organized crime enforcement squad carried out between 400 and 1,000 contract killings for the National Crime Syndicate before being exposed by a turncoat member nicknamed 'Kid Twist.' What was this group called?
Murder, Inc.: American organized crime groups in the 1930s and 1940s.
A Florentine diplomat of the Italian Renaissance, this man wrote a famous political treatise published only after his death and is often called the father of modern political science — who was he?
Niccolò Machiavelli: Florentine statesman, diplomat, and political theorist (1469–1527)

Syrian civil war: 2011–2024 armed conflict in Syria.

Theodoric the Great: King of Italy from 493 to 526. As ruler of the combined Gothic realms, Theodoric controlled an empire stretching from the Atlantic Ocean to the Adriatic Sea.

Walled off to the east and south by the Carpathians and to the west by the Apuseni Mountains, this historical region sits in central Romania and goes by Erdély in Hungarian and Siebenbürgen in German. What is it?
Transylvania: Historical region in Central Europe. Broader definitions of Transylvania also include the western and northwestern Romanian regions of Crișana and Maramureș, and occasionally Banat.
The last man standing in the Year of the Four Emperors, this Roman founded the Flavian dynasty and was the first emperor to rise from an equestrian family. Who was he?
Vespasian: Roman emperor from AD 69 to 79.

War in Abkhazia (1992–1993): Conflict between Georgia and Abkhaz separatists.

A German Army intelligence officer in occupied Warsaw during WWII, this man is credited with saving several Polish Jews, including pianist Władysław Szpilman — his story was dramatized in The Pianist. Who was he?
Wilm Hosenfeld: German army officer (1895–1952) and Righteous among the Nations.

After helping secure the Qing dynasty's abdication, this Chinese general became the Republic's first formal president, only to declare himself emperor in 1915 and abdicate again months later — who was he?
Yuan Shikai: First president of the Republic of China (1859–1916)
Who among these was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
Louis Slotin is a physicist. Louis Alexander Slotin ( SLOHT-in; 1 December 1910 – 30 May 1946) was a Canadian physicist and chemist who took part in the Manhattan Project.
Pick the chemist from these four.
James Lovelock is a chemist. James Ephraim Lovelock (26 July 1919 – 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
What is the atomic number of Unbiunium?
Unbiunium, also known as eka-actinium or element 121, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has symbol Ubu and atomic number 121.
In what year was J. Robert Oppenheimer born?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: In 1941, Oppenheimer was briefed about nuclear weapon design by Australian physicist Mark Oliphant.
In what year did Archimedes die?
Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
In what year was Iron discovered?
Iron is a chemical element; it has symbol Fe (from Latin ferrum 'iron') and atomic number 26.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. Designed by the Soviet Union's Mikoyan-Gurevich bureau, it is an aircraft built primarily using stainless steel.
Which country is Sukhoi Su-57 from?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russia. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Who is credited with discovering Gaussian integral?
Gaussian integral: Leonhard Euler. The integral has a wide range of applications.
Who is credited with discovering Aspirin?
Aspirin: Raffaele Piria. Aspirin is used to treat inflammatory conditions including Kawasaki disease, pericarditis, and rheumatic fever.
Who is credited with discovering Boron?
Boron: Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac. Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.

The active component of vinegar and the second simplest carboxylic acid, this colourless liquid with the formula CH₃COOH has been produced in large quantities since the third millennium BCE. What is this acid?
Acetic acid is an acidic, colourless liquid and organic compound with the chemical formula CH3COOH (also written as CH3CO2H, C2H4O2, or HC2H3O2).
A military pilot who became the first astronaut representing Turkey, he reached the International Space Station on 18 January 2024 aboard the Axiom Mission 3 flight — who is he?
Alper Gezeravcı (born 2 December 1979) is a military pilot and the first Turkish astronaut.
What term describes the discipline of measuring human body dimensions, applied everywhere from ergonomics and architecture to tracking historical living standards?
Anthropometry (from Ancient Greek (nthrpos) 'human' and (mtron) 'measure') refers to the measurement of the human individual.

Distinguished from celestial mechanics by asking what heavenly bodies ARE rather than where they are, this science applies physics and chemistry to the Sun, stars, galaxies, and exoplanets — which discipline?
Astrophysics is a science that applies the methods and principles of physics and chemistry in the study of astronomical objects and phenomena including the universe.
This steroid medication treats conditions ranging from rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis to asthma, and is also given before preterm birth to help speed a baby's lung development — what drug is it?
Betamethasone is a steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.

Derived from Greek words for 'slow' and 'heart', this medical term describes a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute — sometimes a red flag, sometimes just a sign of a well-conditioned athlete. Name the condition?
Bradycardia (brads), meaning "slow", and (karda), meaning "heart", also called bradyarrhythmia, is a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute (BPM).
Caused by an overgrowth of a common yeast, this fungal infection is known as thrush when it affects the mouth and can also cause a genital yeast infection — name the condition?
Candidiasis is a fungal infection due to any species of yeasts in the genus Candida or those that were formerly classified in genus Candida but are now classified in the genus Candidozyma.
Despite no clinical evidence it treats any disease, this daisy-like plant is a staple in calming herbal tea, beer brewing, and even garden ground cover — what is it?
Chamomile (American English) or camomile (British English; see spelling differences) (or) is the common name for several daisy-like plants of the family Asteraceae.
Born near Toulouse, this French inventor is remembered chiefly as an aviation pioneer — though in 1870 he was also an early enthusiast of cycling in France; who was he?
Clément Ader (French; 2 April 1841 - 3 May 1925) was a French inventor and engineer who was born near Toulouse in Muret, Haute-Garonne, and died in Toulouse.
Going by puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther depending on the region, this big cat is the most widely distributed wild land mammal in the Western Hemisphere — what is it?
Cougar (Puma concolor), also called puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther, is a large feline native to the Americas.
Caused by either too little insulin or cells that ignore it, this condition keeps blood sugar stubbornly high and comes chiefly in a type 1 and a type 2 — what is it?
Diabetes is a group of common endocrine diseases characterized by sustained high blood sugar levels.
This social science examines the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services, analyzing everything from individual agents to entire economies. What discipline is this?
Economics is a social science that studies the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.
This class of mental health condition is defined by an enduring, pervasive pattern of behavior, emotion, and thought that deviates from social norms and develops early in life. What is it?
Erythritol is an organic compound, the naturally occurring achiral meso four-carbon sugar alcohol (or polyol).
Which evergreen conifer genus has needle-like leaves attached singly to the branch by a circular base, and cones that stand upright like a cedar's rather than hanging down? What is it?
Fir are evergreen coniferous trees belonging to the genus Abies in the family Pinaceae.
Native to Pacific coastal waters from Alaska to Baja California, this giant burrowing clam can grow a siphon over three feet long and live for more than a century — which creature?
Geoduck (Panopea generosa) is a species of very large saltwater clam in the family Hiatellidae.

These common coastal seabirds, most closely related to terns and skimmers, were once known by an older name still surviving in some English dialects and cognate with the German word Möwe — what birds are they?
Gull (see Taxonomy), are seabirds of the subfamily Larinae.
First identified in 1910, this organic compound is stored in mast cells and basophils and, though not made by classic endocrine glands, still acts as a local hormone — what compound is it?
Histamine is an organic nitrogenous compound found in mammals and many vegetables, fruits and food products.

For decades this University of Virginia psychiatrist ran a Division of Perceptual Studies and gathered evidence that memories — and even bodily features — might carry across lives. Which researcher into reincarnation was he?

Ian Stevenson (October 31, 1918 - February 8, 2007) was a Canadian-born American psychiatrist, the founder and director of the Division of Perceptual Studies at the University of Virginia School of Medicine.

This American scientist co-authored a landmark 1953 paper with Francis Crick proposing the double-helix structure of DNA, building on research by Rosalind Franklin, and shared a 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery — who is he?
James Watson (April 6, 1928 - November 6, 2025) was an American molecular biologist, geneticist, and zoologist.

Sharing the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, this ethologist was among the first to decode the honey bee's waggle dance — a theory greeted with such skepticism that it took decades to be vindicated. Who was he?
Karl von Frisch (20 November 1886 - 12 June 1982) was a German-Austrian ethologist who received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1973, along with Nikolaas Tinbergen and Konrad Lorenz.

This Hungarian-born physicist conceived the nuclear chain reaction in 1933, drafted the famous letter Einstein signed to launch the Manhattan Project, then later petitioned President Truman not to drop the bomb on civilians — who was he?

Leo Szilard (born Le Spitz; February 11, 1898 - May 30, 1964) was a Hungarian-born American physicist, biologist and inventor who made numerous important discoveries in nuclear physics and the biological sciences.
Reclassified in 2021 as part of the order Psocodea alongside booklice and barklice, these tiny wingless parasites cement their eggs to a single host for life — what are they called?
Louse (pl.: lice) is the common name for any member of the infraorder Phthiraptera, which contains nearly 5,000 species of wingless parasitic insects.
Google's employee No. 20 and its first woman software engineer, she later left to run a famous internet company as CEO from 2012 until Verizon bought it — who is she?
Marissa Mayer (born May 30, 1975) is an American business executive, software engineer, and investor who served as president and chief executive officer of Yahoo!
What neurological disorder causes moderate-to-severe, often one-sided headaches, frequently accompanied by nausea, light and sound sensitivity, and sometimes preceded by a sensory 'aura'?
Migraine is a neurological disorder that causes moderate-to-severe headaches. The pain usually affects one side of the head.
With somewhere between 66 and 70 species across nine subfamilies, this carnivore family stretches from tiny weasels all the way up to the wolverine. What is it?
Mustelidae (from Latin mustela, weasel) are a diverse family of carnivoran mammals, including weasels, badgers, otters, sea otters, polecats, martens, grisons and wolverines.

Considered primary if a child has never had a long dry stretch, this common childhood condition — usually a developmental delay rather than an illness — is commonly called bedwetting. What's its clinical name?
Nocturnal enuresis (NE), also informally called bedwetting, is involuntary urination while asleep after the age at which bladder control usually begins.
Derived from an ancient Roman unit called the uncia, this unit of mass equals 1/16 of a pound in its common form, though a heavier 'troy' version weighs precious metals — name the unit?
Ounce is any of several different units of mass, weight, or volume and is derived almost unchanged from the uncia, an Ancient Roman unit of measurement.

This short-acting barbiturate is used as a sedative and anticonvulsant in low doses, but in high doses causes fatal respiratory arrest, making it a drug of choice for both veterinary euthanasia and U.S. executions — what is it?
Pentobarbital (US) or pentobarbitone (British and Australian) is a short-acting barbiturate typically used as a sedative, a preanesthetic, and to control convulsions in emergencies.
Native to Eurasia and identifiable by short, blue-green needles, this member of the pine family goes by several regional common names — name the species (Latin binomial)?
Pinus sylvestris is a species of tree in the pine family Pinaceae that is native to Eurasia.
Split into the strepsirrhines — lemurs and lorisids — and the haplorhines — tarsiers, monkeys and apes — this order ranges in size down to tiny Madame Berthe's — what is it?

Primate is an order of mammals, which is further divided into the strepsirrhines, which include lemurs, galagos, and lorisids; and the haplorhines, which include tarsiers and simians (monkeys and apes).

Founding an organization promoting swadeshi economics against globalization, this Indian social activist later allied with a yoga guru to combine that economic message with the promotion of yoga and Ayurveda — who is he?
Rajiv Dixit (30 November 1967 - 30 November 2010) was an Indian social activist who founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan.

This English X-ray crystallographer's photographs were crucial to unraveling the structure of DNA, yet her contribution went largely unrecognized in her lifetime, earning her posthumous nicknames like "the wronged heroine" — who was she?
Rosalind Franklin (25 July 1920 - 16 April 1958) was an English chemist and X-ray crystallographer.
With segmented bony armor, an upright posture, and a curling prehensile tail, these 46 species of tiny bony fish are cousins to the pipefishes and seadragons — what are they?
Seahorse (also written sea-horse and sea horse) is any of 46 species of small marine bony fish in the genus Hippocampus.
Once placed alone in the genus Uncia before phylogenetics moved it into Panthera, this high-altitude cat ranges across the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas — what is it?
Snow leopard (Panthera uncia) is a species of large cat in the genus Panthera of the family Felidae.
Lacking the powder down that herons and ibises use to clean off fish slime, these bill-clattering wading birds come in 20 living species across six genera — which birds?
Stork are large, long-legged, long-necked wading birds with long, stout bills.

Equal to one weber per square metre, this SI unit of magnetic flux density was adopted in 1960 and named for a Serbian-American electrical engineer, on the proposal of a Slovenian engineer — name this unit?
Tesla (unit) (symbol: T) is the unit of magnetic flux density (B) (also called magnetic B-field) in the International System of Units (SI).
Roughly eight times more potent than an older analogue, this bleeding-control medication is also prescribed for hereditary angioedema — what is it?
Tranexamic acid is a medication used to treat or prevent excessive blood loss from major trauma, postpartum bleeding, surgery, tooth removal, nosebleeds, and heavy menstruation.
This British-American structural biologist shared the 2009 Nobel in Chemistry for revealing the ribosome's structure and later led the Royal Society as president — who is he?
Venki Ramakrishnan (born 1952) is a British-American structural biologist.
Marketed under names like Rompun, this veterinary sedative and alpha-2 adrenergic agonist is often combined with ketamine for animal anesthesia and used as an emetic in cats — what is it?

Xylazine is a structural analog of clonidine and an 2-adrenergic receptor agonist, sold under many trade names worldwide, most notably the Bayer brand name Rompun, as well as Anased, Sedazine and Chanazine.
Caused by a mutation in the FGFR3 gene, this genetic disorder is the most common cause of short stature, marked by shortened limbs, a normal-length torso and a prominent forehead — what is it called?
Achondroplasia: Genetic condition, the most common form of dwarfism.
With wingspans reaching up to eleven and a half feet, which large seabird family ranges across the Southern Ocean and North Pacific but is absent from the North Atlantic?
Albatross: Family of large seabirds. The albatrosses are usually regarded as falling into four genera, but disagreement exists over the number of species.
The heaviest member of its family, this Southeastern U.S. reptile sees males stretch up to 15 feet and tip 1,000 pounds — and it's the larger of just two surviving species in its genus. What is it?
American alligator: Crocodilian native to the Southeastern United States.

Characterized by extreme food restriction and a fear of gaining weight despite being underweight, this eating disorder is described in the DSM-5 as involving a disturbance in how one perceives their own body shape — what's the condition called?
Anorexia nervosa: Eating disorder. Individuals with anorexia nervosa have a fear of gaining weight, despite the fact that they are typically underweight.
Sold under the brand name Abilify, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia, bipolar mania, and irritability linked to autism spectrum disorder — what is it?
Aripiprazole: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Aripiprazole is taken by mouth or via injection into a muscle.
Delivered to the RAF starting in 1956, this delta-wing strategic bomber was considered the most advanced but riskiest of Britain's three V bombers — which aircraft?
Avro Vulcan: British jet-powered delta wing strategic bomber.
A largely self-taught naturalist and astronomer born to a free mother in Maryland, he helped survey the District of Columbia and corresponded with Thomas Jefferson — who was he?
Benjamin Banneker: American scientist, surveyor and farmer (1731–1806)
Despite being just 12 to 20 cm long, this small marine creature's vivid markings flash brighter when it feels threatened, and its bite delivers a neurotoxin called tetrodotoxin — what is it?
Blue-ringed octopus: Four species of mollusk.

Unique among mammals, human females are the only ones to permanently develop this secondary sex organ at puberty rather than just during pregnancy, and it later produces milk via the mammary gland — which body part?
Breast: Part of the female primate torso that has mammary glands.
With the formula CaC2, this industrial compound reacts with trace moisture to give off a garlicky smell and is used to generate acetylene gas in old-fashioned lamps — what is it?
Calcium carbide: Chemical compound. Its main use industrially is in the production of acetylene and calcium cyanamide.
This mammalian order of flesh-eating species is split into cat-like and dog-like suborders, Feliformia and Caniformia, and ranks as the sixth-largest order of mammals — which order?
Carnivora: Order of mammals. Carnivora ( kar-NIV-ər-ə) is an order of placental mammals specialised primarily in eating flesh, whose members are formally referred to as carnivorans.
Known in North America as fireweed and in Britain as rosebay willowherb, this perennial flowering plant thrives across the boreal forests of the Northern Hemisphere — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium: Species of flowering plant in the willowherb family.
Named from Latin words meaning 'around' and 'day,' this roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle appears independently across animals, plants, fungi, and cyanobacteria?
Circadian rhythm: Natural internal process that regulates the sleep-wake cycle.
This bird family contains both doves and pigeons — including the feral rock dove common in cities — spanning 52 genera and 353 species worldwide. What's the family called?
Columbidae: Family of birds. The bird most commonly referred to as "pigeon" is the domestic pigeon, descendant of the wild rock dove, which is a common inhabitant of cities as the feral pigeon.

First published in 1785 by a French physicist, this principle holds that the electrostatic force between two charged particles is proportional to their charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them — which principle is it?
Coulomb's law: Fundamental physical law of electromagnetism.

Originally bred for the hunt and later famous for trotting alongside horse-drawn firehouse carriages, this white breed with dark spots traces its roots to a region on the Adriatic coast — which breed?
Dalmatian dog: Croatian hunting/carriage/coach dog breed.
Known for feigning death when cornered, which genus of cat-sized marsupials includes the only marsupial species found north of Mexico?
Didelphis: Genus of marsupials. The six species in the genus Didelphis, commonly known as Large American opossums, are members of the opossum order, Didelphimorphia.
This plant genus in the mallow family produces the world's most famously pungent fruit, alongside eight other edible-fruit-bearing species — which genus?
Durio: Genus of plants. Several species produce an edible fruit known as durian, the most common species being Durio zibethinus, with eight others producing edible fruit.
Nicknamed the ALX, this Brazilian turboprop light-attack aircraft is assembled in Jacksonville, Florida with an American defense partner for low-threat counter-insurgency missions — which aircraft?
Embraer EMB 314 Super Tucano: Light ground attack and training aircraft.
Odorless, colorless, and dangerously sweet-tasting, this viscous compound goes into polyester fibers and antifreeze — and has even been spotted in outer space. What is it?
Born in 1963, this woman is the daughter of the last Shah of Iran by his third wife — who is she?
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
With a melting point of just under 30 degrees Celsius, this metal will turn to liquid in the palm of your hand — which element?
Gallium: Chemical element with atomic number 31 (Ga)
Found in birds, crocodilians, and earthworms alike, this thick-muscled digestive organ grinds food with the help of swallowed grit — what's it called?
Gizzard: Digestive organ of some animals.
Rising from the ashes of the cancelled F-111B, which variable-sweep-wing Navy fighter first flew in 1970 and deployed aboard USS Enterprise?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat: Carrier-based multi-role fighter aircraft family.
This German physicist was the first to conclusively demonstrate the electromagnetic waves predicted by James Clerk Maxwell's equations — who is he?
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

In this heart condition, the muscle walls, especially the wall between the ventricles, thicken without an obvious cause, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes disrupting its electrical signals — which condition?

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: Enlargement of the heart muscle. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.

This analytical framework describes how overlapping identities like race, gender, and class combine to create unique experiences of discrimination or privilege, and emerged partly as a critique of mainstream feminism — which concept?
Intersectionality: Theory of discrimination. The term intersectionality was coined by Kimberlé Crenshaw in 1989.
A Communist Party member and Stanford-trained psychiatrist, this woman is best remembered for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer, which put her under FBI surveillance. Who is she?
Personal physician to the Buddha and King Bimbisāra in 5th-century BCE Rājagṛha, this 'Medicine King' is still revered by traditional healers across Asia — who is he?

Jīvaka: Personal physician of the Buddha and Indian King Bimbisara. Jīvaka (Pali: Jīvaka Komārabhacca; Sanskrit: Jīvaka Kaumārabhṛtya) was the personal physician (Sanskrit: vaidya) of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisāra.
Named from Greek words for 'hare' and 'form,' this mammalian order splits into rabbits-and-hares on one branch and pikas on the other, totaling around 110 living species — which order?
Formed by cross-linking phenolic precursors, this class of complex organic polymers gives rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in wood and bark — what is it?
Lignin: Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Native to Africa except for one species found only on Madagascar, this small parrot gets its common name from its strong, monogamous pair-bonding behavior — what is it?
Oblate rather than round, with a thin, loose peel that makes it easy to separate into segments, this citrus fruit is sweeter and stronger-tasting than its spherical, hybrid cousin — which fruit?
Mandarin orange: Small citrus fruit. A mandarin orange (Citrus reticulata), often simply called mandarin, is a small, rounded citrus tree fruit.
Its name means 'big tooth,' and this extinct giant mackerel shark — once mistaken for a great white relative — is known only from fragmentary remains. What is it?
Megalodon: Extinct giant shark species. Megalodon probably had a major impact on the structure of marine communities.
Sitting atop the brainstem and linking it to the diencephalon and cerebrum, this structure governs vision, hearing, motor control, and arousal -- what is it called?
Midbrain: Forward-most portion of the brainstem.

Nicknamed the Swiss cheese plant for its perforated leaves, this houseplant native to southern Mexico and Central America produces a fruit that's edible once ripe, despite needle-like calcium oxalate crystals elsewhere in the plant — what is its scientific name?
Monstera deliciosa: Species of plant. Monstera deliciosa, the Swiss cheese plant or split-leaf philodendron, is a species of flowering plant.
Made of the same tough protein as claws, hooves, and horns, this protective plate covers the tip of your fingers and toes — what is it?
Nail (anatomy): Hard keratin protection of digit.
Sold under the brand name Macrobid, this antibacterial drug treats lower urinary tract infections but isn't effective against kidney infections. What is it?
Nitrofurantoin: Antibacterial drug. Nitrofurantoin, sold under the brand name Macrobid among others, is an antibacterial medication of the nitrofuran class.

Sold under the brand name Zofran, this serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist prevents chemotherapy- and surgery-related nausea without the dopamine-blocking side effects that cause muscle restlessness — what is this drug?
Ondansetron: Medication to prevent nausea and vomiting.
Known for its fragrant leaves used to flavor dishes across Southeast Asia, Sri Lanka and Hainanese cuisine, this member of the screwpine genus is prized in many Asian kitchens — which plant?
Pandanus amaryllifolius: Species of tropical plant.
Developed at Abbott Laboratories in 1930 and nicknamed 'yellow jackets' for its brand-name capsule color, this barbiturate is used in veterinary euthanasia and some U.S. executions — what drug is it?

Also known as physiography, this branch of natural science studies the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere — as opposed to the branch focused on the built human environment. Which field of study?
Physical geography: Study of processes and patterns in the natural environment.
This large, structurally diverse family of plant compounds includes flavonoids and tannic acid, some of which were historically used as dyes and for tanning garments — what are they called?
Known by folk names like 'bird cherry' and 'Mayday tree,' this flowering plant in the rose family is native to Europe and northern Asia — what species is it?
Prunus padus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
What term describes an atom, molecule, or ion with at least one unpaired valence electron, making it highly reactive and prone to processes like dimerization or polymerization?
Radical (chemistry): Atom, molecule, or ion that has an unpaired valence electron; typically highly reactive.
Named from Greek words for 'rose' and 'tree,' this flowering shrub genus is Nepal's national flower and includes azaleas as a subgenus — which plant?
Rhododendron: Genus of flowering plants. Azaleas make up two subgenera of Rhododendron.
First identified in November 2002 and traced through civets to horseshoe bats in Yunnan, this viral respiratory disease had an 11% fatality rate before its outbreak ended in 2003 — which disease?
After early family-friendly Christian games found little success, which developer switched to horror in 2014 and created a hit franchise of horror video games?
Scott Cawthon: American video game developer (born 1978)

Adapted from the Army's Black Hawk with folding rotor blades and a hinged tail to fit aboard ships, this twin-engine Navy helicopter handles everything from anti-submarine warfare to medical evacuation — which aircraft?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Sikorsky SH-60 Seahawk: Naval helicopter series of the H-60/S-70 family.

Found in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and northeastern Australia, this large flightless black bird is a close ratite relative of the emu and ostrich, and its Australian population is listed as endangered — which bird?
Southern cassowary: Species of flightless bird. It is one of the three living species of cassowary, alongside the dwarf cassowary and the northern cassowary.
This throat infection causes fever, red tonsils, and swollen neck glands, and can trigger a sandpaper-textured rash known as scarlet fever — which condition?
Streptococcal pharyngitis: Medical condition. It may be spread directly through touching infected sores.
The lone species in its genus, this African-born leguminous tree gives pods of sweet-tangy pulp used in cuisines worldwide, plus a seed oil and even a dye — what is it?
Tamarind: Leguminous tree bearing edible fruit.
First unearthed in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in 1948, this Late Cretaceous giant is known mainly from claw bones over half a meter long, giving it a name meaning 'scythe lizard' — which dinosaur genus?
Therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurid genus from the Late Cretaceous period.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.

A hemiparasitic plant that draws water and nutrients from host trees, this species is central to European Christmas traditions and folklore, and is now studied for possible pharmaceutical use — what plant is it commonly called?
Viscum album: Flowering plant in the mistletoe family Santalaceae.

Caused by the deletion of about 27 genes on chromosome 7, this genetic disorder is known for an unusually outgoing, empathetic personality alongside visual-spatial learning challenges — which condition?
Williams syndrome: Genetic disorder. Williams syndrome (WS), also Williams–Beuren syndrome (WBS), is a genetic disorder that affects many parts of the body.
Fluorine is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for fluorine is F. Fluorine is a chemical element; it has the symbol F and atomic number 9.
What is the chemical symbol for cerium?
The symbol for cerium is Ce. Cerium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ce and atomic number 58, and is a soft, ductile, and silvery-white metal that tarnishes when exposed to air.

Which of these four was born earliest?
Jonathan Glazer (born 1965) is the earliest of the four. Jonathan Glazer (born 26 March 1965) is an English filmmaker.

F. Murray Abraham (born 1939) is the earliest of the four. Murray Abraham (born Murray Abraham; October 24, 1939) is an American actor.
Betty Boop (founded 1930) is the earliest of the four.

Monday Night Football (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.

In what year was Sigourney Weaver born?
Sigourney Weaver: Susan Alexandra "Sigourney" Weaver ( sig-OR-nee; born October 8, 1949) is an American actress.
In what year was Michael Keaton born?
Michael Keaton: Michael John Douglas (born September 5, 1951), known professionally as Michael Keaton, is an American actor.
In what year was Eva Mendes born?
Eva Mendes: Eva de la Caridad Méndez (Spanish: [ˈeβa ðe la kaɾiˈðað ˈmendes]; born March 5, 1974), known professionally as Eva Mendes, is an American former actress.
